item.title: AeroProp-X: An Open-Source, Self-Verifying Method-of-Characteristics Toolkit for Edge-Capable Rocket Nozzle Design and Aerothermodynamic Analysis
item.description: arXiv:2610.20612v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The design of supersonic rocket nozzles by the Method of Characteristics is a mature discipline, yet the software that implements it is frequently either proprietary, heavyweight, or opaque, which limits reproducibility and classroom and field use. This paper presents AeroProp-X, an open-source, dependency-light toolkit that synthesizes shock-free minimum-length nozzle contours and evaluates their ideal aerothermodynamic performance entirely on commodity hardware without graphics acceleration or network access. The central contribution is methodological rather than physical: the planar characteristics solver is made self-verifying by exploiting an exact gas-dynamic invariant, namely that the computed exit wall height ratio must equal the isentropic area ratio at the design Mach number, so that every generated contour reports its own discretization error automatically. We describe the governing theory, the layered software architecture, and the synthesis algorithm, and we validate the implementation against analytic compressible-flow tables and against the expansion ratios of historical flight engines. The solver reproduces tabulated gas-dynamic quantities to table precision and converges to the exact area ratio with relative error below three parts in ten thousand, while remaining small enough to run interactively on an embedded-class processor. We argue that built-in verifiability, dependency minimalism, and explicit scoping of the ideal-flow assumptions together make the tool well suited to education, preliminary design, and reproducible research.
item.dc:creator: Aryuemaan Kumar Chowdhury

item.title: Physics-informed Kolmogorov-Arnold networks (PIKANs) for noise-robust reconstruction of boiling heat flux from infrared measurements
item.description: arXiv:2610.20613v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Recovering a noise-amplified inverse quantity from corrupted boundary data is a recurring problem in physics-informed learning for real-world applications. Specifically, small perturbations in the measured field are magnified through the spatial derivatives needed to reconstruct the target, and hence conventional discretization solvers turn them into large unphysical oscillations. We study this problem through the reconstruction of local time-resolved nucleate-boiling heat flux, which cannot be measured directly and must be inferred from infrared surface temperatures by solving an unsteady three-dimensional heat-conduction problem with sharp and rapidly evolving liquid-vapor interface gradients. We show that neither network architecture nor optimizer alone overcomes the spectral bias that smooths away these interface-scale features, and that the two must be addressed jointly. Our approach combines a Chebyshev physics-informed Kolmogorov-Arnold network (PIKAN) backbone, a quasi-second-order (SOAP) optimizer, and a temperature-annealed residual-based resampling scheme that concentrates collocation points at high-residual interface regions. Trained directly on experimental infrared measurements imposed as a boundary condition, the network resolves high-frequency bubble signatures and the high-flux distribution tail much better than a Fourier-feature PINN of equal size and training budget. In particular, it selectively filters measurement noise while preserving the physically meaningful high-frequency features, suppressing the spurious oscillations that contaminate finite-volume reconstructions and yielding more physically consistent heat-flux estimates from noisy experimental data.
item.dc:creator: Siavash Khodakarami, Parimala Vardhan Vydyula, Aniruddha Bora, Justin A. Weibel, George Em Karniadakis

item.title: Thermodynamically Consistent Machine Learning for Fracture Prediction in Heterogeneous Materials
item.description: arXiv:2610.20614v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Understanding fracture behavior is critical for assessing the structural integrity and longevity. Highly time-consuming physics-based fracture simulations motivate the development of machine-learning-based fracture evolution prediction with surrogate models. However, most existing machine-learning models for fracture prediction operate as black boxes and require large training datasets to generalize reliably. In this work, Thermodynamically Consistent Latent Dynamics Identification (tLaSDI) for parametric systems is introduced to predict fracture patterns and evolution in heterogeneous materials. The model learns the thermodynamic state variable in a lower-dimensional latent space using parametric GENERIC Formalism-Informed Neural Networks (pGFINNs) that enforce key thermodynamic principles, such as total energy conservation and entropy generation. This model embeds physics into the neural network architecture using a hard-constraint method that inherently complies with the underlying thermodynamic principles. The proposed tLaSDI-pGFINNs is further enhanced by a Geometry-Conditioned Autoencoder in learning the geometry configuration for effective geometry-guided learning. The energy and entropy evolution histories demonstrate that the model preserves the thermodynamic constraints on unseen testing samples. The results further show that tLaSDI-pGFINNs can more accurately capture both fracture patterns and the subsequent fracture evolution than the purely data-driven Autoencoder Long Short-Term Memory (AE-LSTM) model.
item.dc:creator: Muhamad Alim, Xiaolong He, Mei-Na Tsao, Chi-Hua Yu, J. S. Chen

item.title: Iterative Neural Variational Solver of Committor Function in Under-damped Langevin Dynamics
item.description: arXiv:2610.20617v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The committor function describes the probability that a stochastic dynamical system, while transitioning between two metastable states, will first reach one state rather than the other. It is a central object in transition path theory, providing the accurate reaction rate and the characterization of the transition mechanism through reactive probability flux and the transition state ensemble. While the numerical methods for this function are well studied for over-damped Langevin dynamics where the friction damping coefficient goes to infinity, its computation in the general under-damped case remains an open challenge due to the lack of a variational structure in the underlying backward Kolmogorov equation. This restricts the quantitative investigation of the impact of the finite damping coefficient on rare transitions in real systems. In this work, by decomposing the infinitesimal generator of the underdamped Langevin dynamics into a self-adjoint and a skew-adjoint part, we develop an iterative scheme in which each subproblem has a variational form and can be solved efficiently using neural networks. Fundamentally, this approach can be viewed as a generalized Concus-Golub-Widlund (CGW) splitting method and each subproblem has a variational form, which can be solved efficiently. This iterative scheme also has the flexibility of introducing a preconditioning operator associated with a new overdamped Langevin dynamics, which naturally leads to the design of enhanced adaptive sampling for the subproblems. We validate the efficiency and accuracy of our method on benchmark systems including a one-dimensional double-well potential, the Muller-Brown potential, and alanine dipeptide. The proposed iterative variational framework provides a practical and extensible numerical tool for probing rare transition events in Langevin dynamics across varying damping coefficients.
item.dc:creator: Tiejun Li, Zhaoqi Liu, Xiang Zhou

item.title: pcNN-SN: a physics-enhanced predictor-corrector neural network algorithm coupled with the discrete ordinates method for neutron transport equations
item.description: arXiv:2610.20619v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Super-resolution machine learning methods hold promise for addressing the high computational costs associated with high-dimensional features in traditional transport simulations. This paper proposes a physics-enhanced neural network coupling algorithm for discrete ordinates (SN) transport calculations. Based on high- and low-accuracy data, we develop a predictor-corrector neural network (pcNN) to predict correction factors for coarse-grid solutions. Based on transport equations, local physical features containing subgrid-scale information are selected as network inputs. Dimensionless transformation of physical quantities reduces the input space dimensionality and narrows parameter distributions, facilitating network training. Physical constraints are incorporated into the network model, and the corrected solution retains its original conservation properties. pcNN and SN transport sweeps are internally coupled, and numerical solutions are corrected online. Numerical results demonstrate that this algorithm can effectively improve coarse-grid solutions to achieve a level of accuracy comparable to that of fine-grid results. The physics-based network design enables the model to demonstrate a certain degree of reusability under different computational conditions. Compared to mesh refinement, the pcNN-SN algorithm reduces the computation time for the three-dimensional test problem by more than 60%.
item.dc:creator: Cong Liu, Junxia Wei, Shuai Wang, Heng Yong

item.title: Representation-split Carleman lattice Boltzmann with near-unit step success probability on quantum computers
item.description: arXiv:2610.20620v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Carleman lattice Boltzmann method replaces the quadratic collision of the lattice Boltzmann equation by a linear map on a lifted state. Existing block encodings of this map succeed with probability $10^{-5}$ to $10^{-2}$ per step, so that the probability of a multi-step evolution decays exponentially with the number of steps. This study develops multi-relaxation-time Carleman lattice Boltzmann, a representation split in which the Carleman-lifted collision is performed in a moment basis on the amplitude-encoded state, while streaming remains a permutation in population space. The level-2 hierarchy closes under collision but not under streaming, which generates the work of pressure, advection and stress on the momentum flux. The state therefore remains the full pair array, and the moment representation is an orthogonal change of basis of the population one, with identical dynamics and truncation error. The operator to be block encoded changes with the basis, and with it the success probability of a quantum step. In the weighted Hermite basis with the amplitude encoding $f_i/\sqrt{w_i}$, the relaxation is a diagonal operator of norm one, and the level-2 collision stage becomes this diagonal plus a sparse coupling from products of conserved moments. A structured block encoding of this form raises the single-step success probability on the D2Q9 lattice from $10^{-2}$ for the best population encoding to 0.98. With the pair sector in relative coordinates and scaled, one step requires $O(\log^2 N)$ Toffoli gates and is verified by statevector simulation. The encoding and readout overhead of a $T$-step run is then polynomial in $T$ and $N$ rather than accumulating a factor $p^T$. For resolved flows, the remaining exponential loss in coherent multi-step Carleman lattice Boltzmann evolution is set by the non-equilibrium norm relaxed by dissipation rather than by the block encoding.
item.dc:creator: Hua-Dong Yao, Sauro Succi

item.title: On the Assessment of Domain Decomposition Approaches in Extended Physics-Informed Neural Networks for the Shock-Dominated Burgers Equation
item.description: arXiv:2610.20621v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) provide a mesh-free framework for solving partial differential equations but often struggle with sharp gradients and shock-dominated solutions. Extended Physics-Informed Neural Networks (XPINNs) address this challenge through domain decomposition; however, the effects of decomposition design, overlap, and local network capacity on solution accuracy remain insufficiently characterized. This work presents a systematic assessment of domain decomposition configurations for XPINNs applied to the one-dimensional viscous Burgers equation ($\nu=0.01/\pi$). We compare a standard PINN, a conventional XPINN, a shock-focused XPINN with increased network capacity in the shock-containing subdomain, and overlapping XPINNs with different overlap widths. All configurations are trained using a common protocol based on Adam, L-BFGS refinement, and ten Residual-based Adaptive Refinement (RAR) cycles. Performance is evaluated against a reference solution using global and shock-region relative $L_2$ and $L_\infty$ errors, maximum PDE residuals, and interface continuity errors. The results show that decomposition design strongly affects XPINN accuracy and shock resolution. Among the overlapping configurations, the smallest overlap provides the best accuracy, while larger overlaps degrade performance. The shock-focused XPINN achieves the lowest overall solution errors, indicating that increased local network capacity can provide greater benefit than increasing overlap alone. RAR produces the largest improvements during early refinement stages, followed by increasingly non-monotonic changes in accuracy. These findings highlight the importance of jointly considering decomposition, interface coupling, network capacity, and adaptive refinement for shock-dominated problems.
item.dc:creator: Andr\'es F. Bola\~nos-Acosta, Juli\'an C. Restrepo

item.title: Second-Order Homogenization of Particulate Elastomeric Composites for Structural-Scale Damage Analysis
item.description: arXiv:2610.20624v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Damage prediction in particulate elastomeric composites is challenging due to the strong material heterogeneity, nearly incompressible behavior of the matrix, and the presence of localized stress concentrations arising from matrix-inclusion interactions. In the present work, a computational framework is developed for damage propagation analysis of particulate elastomeric composite structures. The effective constitutive response of the heterogeneous material is first determined using the second-order homogenization method. The resulting homogenized response is subsequently used to identify equivalent hyperelastic material parameters for structural simulations. A three-parameter isotropic damage model is incorporated to capture damage-induced softening. A mixed displacement-pressure finite element formulation, is used to alleviate volumetric locking associated with nearly incompressible property of elastomers. The proposed framework is validated through full-scale simulations and homogenized response involving composites with varying inclusion volume fractions. Numerical investigations demonstrate that the homogenized models is able to reproduce the global force-displacement response within 2% error and damage evolution characteristics of the heterogeneous composites while significantly reducing the computational cost.
item.dc:creator: Krishna Murthy Pabbu, Tarkes Dora Pallicity, Nelson Muthu

item.title: Energy-Stable Parametric Operator Inference across Regime Transitions: Application to Unconfined Buoyant Plumes in Stratified Ambients
item.description: arXiv:2610.20626v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Buoyant plumes in stratified ambients arise in wildfire smoke transport, ventilation, and pollutant dispersion, where many-query prediction requires models that stay accurate and stable as the dynamics transition from free rise to internal-wave trapping. Operator Inference (OpInf) learns polynomial reduced models from snapshots, and the Boussinesq plume depends affinely on the squared buoyancy frequency $N^2$. However, this compatibility masks two stability gaps: a single affine operator family can distort the per-parameter dynamics into unstable spectra, and for quadratic OpInf models, finite-time blowup is governed by a cubic energy injection channel from the inferred quadratic operator. To address these gaps, we develop cyclic-skew regime-bridged OpInf (CR-OpInf). We derive an affine-inadequacy diagnostic that links the departure from a shared affine family to destabilizing spectral drift before integration. In place of the shared affine fit, we interpolate per-parameter operators with a Gaussian kernel. We also extend the cyclic-skew quadratic constraint to the buoyancy-source-forced parametric setting, closing the cubic energy channel and isolating this closure as the boundedness mechanism. We further introduce a regime-bridging basis split that resolves free rise and trapped intrusion structures while preserving the cyclic-skew structure under convex interpolation. Applied to an unconfined Boussinesq plume and a viscous Burgers problem spanning a smooth-to-shock transition, CR-OpInf remains bounded for five training horizons, avoids the divergence of affine and unconstrained variants, tracks the plume rise, and recovers stratification-dependent rise scaling at moderate horizons. To our knowledge, this is the first parametric OpInf study of an unconfined stratified plume.
item.dc:creator: Youngjun Kwon, Abdollah Shafieezadeh

item.title: BBun: an unsteady vortex-ring panel method for interacting lifting bodies, box wings and propellers
item.description: arXiv:2610.20629v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This report documents BBun (Blunt Body unsteady), a low-order code for the unsteady potential flow around one or more interacting three-dimensional bodies. The bodies are represented by vortex rings (piecewise-constant doublets) with a Neumann boundary condition; free vortex sheets are shed from the trailing edges and, optionally, from the tips, and convected in time, with an implicit unsteady Kutta condition. The report describes the choices that make the discretization consistent and convergent (a single desingularized kernel per wake line, a bordered factorization of the singular Neumann problem, interior velocity conditions for the nearly singular mode of ring-shaped bodies, the detection of the separation lines from the grid connectivity) and the extensions to several bodies, box wings, symmetric configurations (image method), non-lifting bodies, rigidly rotating bodies (propellers), the unsteady Bernoulli equation, a wake-body collision treatment and a strip-wise integral boundary layer. The verification and validation are reported in full: potential flow around a sphere, sensitivity and grid convergence, the two-dimensional limit, an independent vortex-lattice method, the NACA 0015 wing of McAlister and Takahashi (loads and chordwise pressures), the NACA 0012 profile drag, the biplane of Knight and Noyes, Prandtl's best wing system, Wagner's function and blade-element momentum theory for a propeller. A complete aircraft with counter-rotating tractor propellers illustrates the use of the code.
item.dc:creator: Daniele Peri

item.title: Thermochemically Constrained Multiscale Laplace Neural Operator to Learn Stiff Chemical Kinetics with Conditional Diffusion Model Sampling
item.description: arXiv:2610.20643v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Stiff chemical kinetics is a major computational bottleneck in reacting-flow simulations, while data-driven solvers remain sensitive to training-state coverage and chemical dynamics. This work combines conditional diffusion sampling with a thermochemically constrained multiscale Laplace neural operator (TC-MLNO) for chemistry ODE integration. The diffusion model learns the equivalence-ratio-conditioned joint distribution of temperature and species from low-dimensional flame data, augmenting the state space without independent perturbations. TC-MLNO represents transient, non-periodic responses through pole-residue Laplace layers and assigns fast, medium, and slow species to separate branches. Thermochemical constraints are imposed through losses for mass and elemental conservation and heat release rate. The framework is evaluated in 1D premixed flames, a 2D developing jet, and a 3D turbulent burner flame. With equal-sized datasets, diffusion sampling reduces the 95th-percentile distance to the base flame manifold by up to 37.5% and the a posteriori full-species macro-average error by up to 92.7% versus random sampling, especially for minor species and radicals. TC-LNO yields smaller errors than the DeepONet baseline for 84.9% of retained modes and reduces the 95th-percentile error for the most attenuated modes from 0.372 to 0.081. In multidimensional flames, TC-MLNO better preserves reaction-zone locations, heat-release structures, and chemically sensitive species than DeepONet. Errors of representative radical and nitrogen-containing species in the 3D flame decrease by 88.0%-88.9%. Compared with direct CVODE integration, TC-MLNO reduces mean chemistry and total solution times by 90.1% and 62.6%, respectively. These results show that distribution-aware sampling and Laplace neural operator learning provide an accurate and efficient alternative for stiff chemical ODE integration.
item.dc:creator: Dong Yang, Xiongbo Duan, Min Zhang, Yuqiang Li

item.title: Global-in-time Spectral Duhamel-Picard Method for Post-Exposure Bake Simulation and Physics-Informed Neural Operators for EUV Lithography
item.description: arXiv:2610.20655v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present a global-in-time spectral Duhamel-Picard method with polynomial expansions for post-exposure bake (PEB) simulation. The coupled acid-quencher reaction-diffusion equations are reformulated as nonlinear Volterra integral equations using the Duhamel principle. Full trajectories are represented by finite polynomial expansions, with temporal coefficient fields determined over the bake interval by Anderson-accelerated Picard iteration, thereby avoiding sequential time marching. In 3-D PEB simulations, we employ Chebyshev and Legendre temporal bases while evaluating the Duhamel integrals using the corresponding Gaussian quadrature rules. We demonstrate that the proposed method simulates a large domain of $1200\times1200\times100$ voxels on the order of one minute. The representation is further incorporated into a physics-informed neural operator (PINO) with a mixed-transform variant of a factorized Fourier neural operator, which is trained without precomputed solution trajectories. Together, the integral formulation and its PINO extension enable accelerated, time-marching-free prediction of concentration fields at arbitrary times within the bake interval.
item.dc:creator: Doyun Kim, Mircea Dusa, Werner Gilijns, Philippe Leray

item.title: An implicit multiscale solver for steady kinetic equations based on wave-particle decomposition
item.description: arXiv:2610.20660v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Steady kinetic computations require accurate transport on meshes that do not resolve the mean free path and efficient removal of slowly decaying macroscopic errors. We develop a closed wave-particle decomposition (WPD) and a residual-based implicit solver for this problem. The wave accumulates only the Maxwellian along a local characteristic horizon and is determined by the conservative variables; the particle carries the kinetic complement and collision remainder. Under moment compatibility, the closed system is equivalent to the kinetic equation. For the Bhatnagar-Gross-Krook and Shakhov models, a hydrodynamic expansion gives the wave and particle contributions to the Euler and Navier-Stokes fluxes. The implicit iteration couples macroscopic prediction to microscopic correction through a discrete endpoint term and synchronizes the conservative moments after each accepted correction. Its stationary states satisfy the target discrete kinetic equation independently of the iteration controls. Formal analysis gives the smooth fixed-mesh fluid limit. Linear model analysis relates convergence to the horizon-to-relaxation ratio, incomplete macroscopic solves and explicit collision remainders. One- and two-dimensional computations of a normal shock, internal flows and hypersonic external flows test these properties across rarefied and continuum regimes. The results show kinetic fidelity and substantial reductions in iteration counts and wall time relative to the conventional iterative scheme near the continuum limit. Collision-model comparisons and parameter studies support the predicted convergence mechanisms.
item.dc:creator: Chang Liu, Kun Xu

item.title: A differentiable PCA-GPR surrogate framework for full-transient Bayesian inverse uncertainty quantification of black-box nuclear thermal-hydraulic systems
item.description: arXiv:2610.20978v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Complex transient energy systems require uncertainty-quantified predictions, but Bayesian inverse uncertainty quantification (IUQ) is often impractical because posterior sampling with high-fidelity system codes requires many expensive full-transient simulations. This study develops a surrogate-assisted Bayesian IUQ framework that makes full-time-series calibration practical for the NACIE heavy-liquid-metal natural-circulation loop. The key innovation is to transform a black-box transient simulator into a differentiable probabilistic emulator by combining principal component analysis with Gaussian process regression (PCA--GPR). The surrogate reconstructs complete multichannel temperature and mass-flow histories from a compact latent representation, preserving dominant temporal and cross-channel correlations while enabling automatic differentiation of the log posterior. This allows both gradient-free ensemble slice sampling and gradient-informed sampling with the No-U-Turn Sampler and Microcanonical Langevin Monte Carlo. Five principal components capture more than 99\% of the output variance, and the surrogate achieves normalized root-mean-square errors below 2\%. Compared with direct Flownex SE evaluations, the surrogate reduces likelihood-evaluation cost by approximately 3000-fold while preserving posterior statistics and correlations. Posterior predictive analyses show reduced bias, narrower intervals, and improved agreement with measurements and independent validation.
item.dc:creator: Zikang Yaoa, Eugene Yeea, Fue-Sang Lien

item.title: A Scalable Sharp-Interface Immersed Boundary Method for Moving Boundary Flow Simulation on Multi-GPU Systems
item.description: arXiv:2610.21032v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Sharp-interface immersed boundary methods provide a versatile framework for simulating flows with complex moving boundaries, but their irregular data structures, dynamic sparsity, and discontinuous pressure operators present significant challenges for efficient multi-GPU implementation. This work presents a fully GPU-native, multi-GPU acceleration of the sharp-interface immersed boundary solver, ViCar3D. The implementation combines a hybrid OpenACC/CUDA programming model with a matrix decomposition that isolates dynamically changing immersed-boundary operators, GPU-optimized geometric kernels, asynchronous dual-stream sparse matrix--vector execution, and a symmetric-memory-based sparse communication strategy. A GPU-oriented iterative solver employing a preconditioned stabilized bi-conjugate gradient (BiCGStab) method is developed to efficiently treat the pressure Poisson equation on highly stretched Cartesian grids. The resulting framework preserves the accuracy and versatility of the original solver while delivering substantial acceleration and scalability for simulations involving complex moving and deforming immersed boundaries, thereby extending the applicability of sharp-interface immersed boundary methods to extreme-scale computational fluid dynamics.
item.dc:creator: Sushrut Kumar, Joshua Romero, Massimiliano Fatica, Jung-Hee Seo, Rajat Mittal

item.title: RAT-EC: Introducing a New Open-Source 3D Volume-Integral Eddy-Current Module
item.description: arXiv:2610.21315v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present RAT-EC, an open-source volume-integral eddy-current module for unstructured meshes, driven in the time domain by coils of arbitrary winding geometry. It is the first openly available code of this kind and part of the open-source RAT suite. Because only the conductor is meshed, neither the surrounding air nor an artificial outer boundary has to be modelled, which simplifies model preparation and brings problems with thin gaps and intricate air regions within reach of standard hardware. The formulation combines a semi-analytical evaluation of the singular and near-singular inductance terms, a multi-level fast multipole method that accelerates both the far-field inductance action and the coil field, topology-aware constraints for multiply connected conductors, and a matrix-free, GPU-accelerated time integration. The implementation is verified against closed-form solutions for a conducting sphere and a conducting ring, and is validated on the TEAM-7 benchmark. At 50 Hz, RAT-EC reproduces the measured field as accurately as finite-element solutions. At 200 Hz, it agrees with a converged finite-element model, but both deviate from published measurements, which suggests that this benchmark point should be re-examined. RAT-EC provides an open platform for volume-integral eddy-current simulation and method development.
item.dc:creator: Daniel Mayr, Jeroen van Nugteren, Julien Dular, Mariusz Wozniak, Jasmin Smajic, Juerg Leuthold

item.title: Analytically Benchmarked Spatial and Temporal Discretization Guidelines for Finite Element Simulation of Thermal Waves
item.description: arXiv:2610.20938v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Finite element simulation is widely used to design and interpret thermal wave-based measurement systems. The accuracy of the results obtained from such simulations depends on how finely the model is resolved in space and time. The discretization resolution is often chosen case by case rather than following a well-defined guideline. This work recommends a discretization protocol for finite element simulation of thermal waves where the spatial discretization is scaled to the thermal diffusion length and the temporal discretization to the number of time steps per cycle. The associated discretization errors are quantified using three benchmark problems of increasing complexity. The spatial phase error converges at second order in the element size, reaching 0.14 degrees at ten elements per diffusion length, whereas the temporal error decreases only at first order in the number of time steps per cycle; thus, the time step can be set from a target phase tolerance $\epsilon$. Each error is assessed against a reference that isolates it. The benchmark case with subsurface defects shows the consequence of violating the recommended discretization protocol.
item.dc:creator: Kaushal Arun Pareek, Daniel May, Peter Meszmer, Bernhard Wunderle, Mohamad Abo Ras

item.title: Algebraic coefficients of fractional parentage for three particles in the oscillator Jacobi basis
item.description: arXiv:2610.21385v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We present a closed-form construction of the orbital coefficients of fractional parentage (CFP) of three identical particles in the translationally invariant harmonic oscillator (HO) Jacobi basis. These are usually obtained by numerically diagonalizing a permutation operator in every energy-angular-momentum block. We show this diagonalization is unnecessary. Dressing the class operator $P_{13} + P_{23}$ with the single unitary $W = H^1 \Phi$ -- a fixed complexification followed by the HO bracket with mass parameter $d=1$ -- turns it into the label swap times an integer. Every CFP is then the single ket $|K_{i,s}\rangle = 2Q^s W^\dagger|i\rangle$ -- a 2-scaled, sign-decorated column of the $d=1$ bracket restricted to one $e_2$-parity of the labels -- whose norm, $1 + s\langle i | J | i \rangle$, is itself a single matrix element. The same $W$ carries label parity into swap symmetry, $W Q^s W^\dagger = R^s$, making the bookkeeping collapse. The eigenvalues are exact integers $\pm 2$ and $\pm 1$ labeling the $S(3)$ symmetry classes. The construction is uniform in $E$, $L$ and symmetry class, reducing CFP-specific work from $O(n^3)$ to $O(n^2)$ in block dimension. An eigensolver remains only inside the bracket engine supplying $H^1$, where all residual numerical error originates. We implement this on an SU(3)-basis bracket engine, checking all 1301 blocks up to $E=50$ (912 366 CFPs, largest block $2907 \times 2907$): the $S(3)$ class assignment is exact everywhere. The residual numerical error (entirely the bracket engine's) stays below $10^{-8}$ for $E \leq 35$, restoring to $\leq 10^{-22}$ via a quadruple-precision build beyond that. We further validate against independently generated antisymmetrization data of a production three-nucleon code, including the $^3$He ground-state energy.
item.dc:creator: A. Step\v{s}ys, S. Mickevi\v{c}ius, D. Germanas

item.title: Imaging defects in two-dimensional crystals by convergent beam electron diffraction
item.description: arXiv:2610.21542v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Convergent beam electron diffraction (CBED), recently demonstrated on two-dimensional (2D) materials, offers a number of interesting applications such as imaging atomic in- and out-of plane shifts, interlayer distances, and individual adsorbates. In this study, we show how CBED allows for atomic-precision imaging of individual defects in 2D materials using one single-shot intensity measurement. In combination with structural calculations using density functional theory, we present simulated CBED patterns for various defects in graphene, each of which exhibits a unique fingerprint distribution. We also show how atomic positions, including the individual atomic defects in graphene, can be reconstructed by iterative phase retrieval from a single CBED pattern.
item.dc:creator: Tatiana Latychevskaia, Pengru Huang, Kostya S. Novoselov

item.title: Thermal Confinement in Plasmonic Nanoparticles under Generalised Pulsed Illumination
item.description: arXiv:2610.21698v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Thermal confinement is a key parameter in photothermal applications, as it determines the spatial extent of the region affected by the generated heat. In this work, we develop a numerical treatment to quantify thermal confinement in spherical plasmonic nanoparticles under excitation conditions ranging from ultrashort pulses to the continuous-wave regime. The model combines generalized optical heating with a finite-difference solution of the transient heat equation and explicitly accounts for finite interfacial thermal conductance. To characterize the spatial distribution of heat, we introduce a thermal confinement radius defined from the temporal temperature envelope in the surrounding medium. We demonstrate that pulse duration acts as a highly effective, tuneable parameter to govern thermal confinement. Notably, we quantitatively show that finite interfacial thermal conductance can induce deviations of up to 20% in the spatial confinement radius and over 60% in the transient thermal construct under ultrashort excitation. By comparing the characteristic dimensions of representative targeting ligands with the resulting thermal-confinement length scales, we show how pulse duration can be precisely tailored to control target heating. These results provide a unified framework for predicting nanoscale heat localization paving the way for the rational design of high precision thermoplasmonic applications.
item.dc:creator: Javier Gonz\'alez-Colsa, Dolores Ortiz, Jos\'e Mar\'ia Saiz, Alfredo Franco, Francisco Gonz\'alez, Fernando Bresme, Pablo Albella

item.title: Lossy Lorentz boosts at ultra-relativistic energies: Numerical study and source survey of high-energy physics software
item.description: arXiv:2610.21897v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Most high-energy-physics software packages implement Lorentz boosts for themselves. At sufficiently large boosts, these routines can return finite, plausible-looking four-vectors whose invariant masses and rest-frame properties are no longer accurate. We survey implementations in widely used collider and air-shower software and compare representative algorithms in three numerical tests. We find that the main problem is usually information discarded by the representation, rather than the arithmetic of the boost formula. Information can be lost when a boost is specified only by its velocity, and again when the result is stored only through Cartesian components. Richer boost input prevents the first loss, while retaining light-cone coordinates prevents the second. Ordinary hard processes at present colliders are safe in double precision; the relevant regimes are low-mass systems, highly boosted auxiliary frames, single-precision particle records and air-shower simulations. Extreme scale hierarchies in parton-shower accuracy tests and ultra-heavy particle decays provide still more demanding cases.
item.dc:creator: Christian Bierlich

item.title: VoroTypes: automated enumeration of Voronoi cell topologies for structural identification of complex crystals in atomistic simulations
item.description: arXiv:2610.21911v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: VoroTypes enumerates, for an arbitrary crystal structure, the complete family of Voronoi cell topologies that can arise under small generic perturbations of atomic positions, and exports it as a topological filter for the VoroTop framework. This extends per-atom structural identification in molecular dynamics simulations, previously limited to a handful of simple reference structures, to complex crystals such as Frank--Kasper and Laves phases, with per-sublattice resolution. The package takes a standard crystallographic description (a CIF or POSCAR file) as input, applies exact symmetry reduction and validity pruning to accelerate the enumeration, and produces filters that load directly into the standalone VoroTop program or into OVITO. A library of pre-computed filters covers over a thousand structures from the Materials Project.
item.dc:creator: Emanuel A. Lazar, Chris H. Rycroft

item.title: Ordinal-pattern transition networks as a symbolic substrate for reservoir computing
item.description: arXiv:2610.21973v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Reservoir computing has established itself as a computationally efficient alternative to fully trained recurrent neural networks using a fixed high-dimensional nonlinear substrate to map temporal input into a feature space for a simple readout. Here, we argue that reservoir computing can be realized entirely within a coarse-grained, symbolic state space, and that constrained random walks on ordinal-pattern transition networks provide a natural instance of this realization, replacing the reservoir's continuous state space with a discrete and directly data-derived one. We develop a formal correspondence between the two frameworks, show that the echo-state property has a natural discrete analog in the ergodicity and spectral gap of the walk's underlying Markov chain, and illustrate the correspondence with a minimal example and an empirical one-step-ahead prediction task evaluated across five paradigmatic model systems. These systems exhibit dynamics that correspond to strictly periodic, quasiperiodic, chaotic, or stochastic signals. We argue that this symbolic reservoir perspective allows a redefinition of the reservoir substrate itself, replacing the requirement of a continuous, randomly generated dynamical system with any sufficiently ergodic, data-derived symbolic process. This opens a route toward interpretable, data-adaptive reservoirs whose internal structure is inferred rather than randomly assigned, with implications for surrogate-data methods and reservoir design more broadly.
item.dc:creator: Max Potratzki, Thomas G. de Jong, Michael Small, Timo Br\"ohl

item.title: The importance of tensor handling and implementation of physics-informed DeepONets
item.description: arXiv:2610.22157v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) reduce or eliminate the need for large labelled datasets by enforcing governing equations during training. Physics-informed Deep Operator Networks (PI-DeepONets) extend this approach to learning solution operators, enabling rapid prediction across families of problems. Despite these advantages, we show that their application to higher-dimensional problems remains limited by the computational cost of training. To address this issue, we propose a modified PI-DeepONet architecture that reduces this cost by removing redundancy in how the Branch network processes input functions across collocation points. The proposed formulation is mathematically equivalent to the original architecture but reduces input tensor sizes and the number of Branch network evaluations. We analyse the computational complexity of both architectures and derive theoretical scaling laws for training time with respect to the number of collocation points and input functions. The proposed architecture is evaluated on 1D, 2D, and 3D linear advection problems. In all cases, it achieves comparable predictive accuracy to the original PI-DeepONet while consistently reducing training time. In 2D experiments, a maximum speed-up of $3.75\times$ is observed, with empirical training-time scaling agreeing with the predicted linear dependence on collocation points and input functions. Furthermore, training a 3D model on an NVIDIA A100 GPU is only feasible using the proposed architecture, as the original formulation exceeds memory limits. These results demonstrate that careful consideration of how PI-DeepONets are implemented can yield substantial gains, enhancing the practical performance of PI-DeepONets and enabling their application to otherwise intractable physics-informed learning problems.
item.dc:creator: Nahum Banks, Gustavo A. M. de Almeida, Sergio Maldonado

item.title: Feature-preserving Latent-EnKF for Data Assimilation of Flows with Shocks
item.description: arXiv:2606.12559v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The ensemble Kalman filter (EnKF) is widely adopted for sequential data assimilation, but fails for solutions with discontinuities, such as shocks in compressible flows. For ensembles with uncertainty in discontinuity location, the EnKF analysis can lose physical consistency, which can be viewed through three lenses: (i) bimodal pointwise statistics in the forecast ensemble, (ii) mixed-sign analysis weights in the affine superposition of forecast members, and (iii) spatially distributed Kalman-gain profiles that modify the state around a discontinuity rather than translating it coherently. In order to preserve flow features in the analysis state and, as such, maintain physical consistency, a feature-preserving latent-EnKF is introduced. The proposed method performs the ensemble update in a low-dimensional latent space learned by a coordinate-conditioned auto-decoder. The latent representation retains near-Gaussian ensemble statistics and provides coordinates in which flow features vary coherently across the forecast ensemble. The EnKF updates performed on the latent codes are decoded into coherent changes in the represented flow features, translating shocks through coordinate morphing rather than superposing them at displaced locations. The corresponding Kalman-gain profiles generated by the latent-EnKF exhibit an approximately step-like variation across the discontinuities, allowing the fronts to translate while preserving sharp features and monotonicity. Sod shock-tube, Mach~2 shock-cylinder, and immersed-body shape-inference tests with sparse, noisy observations demonstrate accurate recovery of shocks and contact discontinuities without spurious oscillations.
item.dc:creator: Hemanth Chandravamsi, Hangchuan Hu, Ponkrshnan Thiagarajan, Tamer A. Zaki

item.title: Braided endovascular implants for intracranial aneurysms: mechanics, hemodynamics, and clinical translation
item.description: arXiv:2609.18544v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Endovascular implants prevent intracranial aneurysm rupture by altering the mechanical and hemodynamic environment at the aneurysm neck. Yet many in silico workflows prescribe or reconstruct the post-deployment geometry before computing flow, leaving unresolved the mechanics that create the clinically relevant interface. Here we review braided intraluminal flow diverters, intrasaccular devices, and emerging flow-disruption concepts across deployment mechanics, inter-wire and wire-wall contact, superelasticity, wall apposition, pore geometry, computational fluid dynamics, and fluid-structure interaction. We connect these modeling choices to neck coverage, malapposition, migration, deformation, and durability, and distinguish established evidence from mechanistic inference and prospective hypotheses. We argue that model fidelity should match the clinical question: prescribed or fast placement may support screening, whereas questions of coverage, apposition, compaction, and migration benefit from mechanically plausible deployment states. An interface-resolved mechanics-to-flow framework, supported by measurable validation targets and standardized reporting, could improve device design and enable more reliable patient-specific treatment planning.
item.dc:creator: Ratnadeep Pramanik, Duygu Dengiz, Mariya S. Pravdivtseva, Martin Frank, Ivo Steinbrecher, Prasanth Velvaluri, Matthias Mayr, Philipp Berg, Sylvia Saalfeld, Naomi Larsen, Olav Jansen, Alexander Popp

item.title: LAO+: Focused, Multi-Replica Accelerated Orthogonal Sampling for Robust Binding Free Energy Predictions
item.description: arXiv:2610.20436v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We introduce Lambda-ABF-OPES+ ($\text{LAO+}$), a multi-replica framework for absolute binding free energy (ABFE) calculations that accelerates both the alchemical transformation and the slow ``orthogonal'' motions coupled to it. At the core of $\text{LAO+}$ is a partitioned $\lambda$-dynamics scheme that concentrates sampling on the abrupt rehydration of the binding pocket, the main bottleneck of ligand decoupling, while Hamiltonian replica exchange relays configurations along the entire alchemical path. This drives a fourfold gain in convergence speed for the rate-limiting leg over our previous $\text{LAO}$ method, which was itself up to ninefold faster than Lambda-ABF, an overall gain of up to $\sim$36-fold. Applied to 28 protein--ligand complexes across five targets, $\text{LAO+}$ achieves a root-mean-square error of 0.83~kcal~mol$^{-1}$ and a correlation of 0.87 with experiment from only 63~ns of sampling per ligand. Moreover, dedicated reservoir replicas accelerate any slow degree of freedom that can be described by a collective variable. We demonstrate this by recovering hidden protein and ligand conformational states, for example in T4 lysozyme, BRD4 and JNK1. Together, these advances make accurate ABFE calculations practical for drug discovery.
item.dc:creator: Narjes Ansari, Florent H\'edin, J\'er\^ome H\'enin, Jean-Philip Piquemal, Louis Lagard\`ere

item.title: Grain Boundary Anisotropy and Its Influence on Helium Bubble Nucleation, Growth, and Decohesion in Polycrystalline Iron
item.description: arXiv:2509.07197v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The accumulation of helium bubbles at grain boundaries (GBs) critically degrades the mechanical integrity of structural materials in nuclear reactors. While GBs act as sinks for radiation-induced defects, their inherent structural anisotropy leads to complex helium bubble evolution behaviors that remain poorly understood. This work integrates accelerated molecular dynamics simulations and a novel atomic-scale metric, the flexibility volume (V_f), to establish the interplay between GB character, helium segregation, and bubble growth mechanisms in body-centered cubic iron. We demonstrate that V_f, which incorporates both local atomic volume and vibrational properties, qualitatively predicts deformation propensity. Our results reveal that the atomic-scale segregation energy landscape dictates initial helium clustering and subsequent bubble morphology, with low-energy channels in tilt {\Sigma}5 boundary facilitating one-dimensional migration while isolated deep traps in twist {\Sigma}13 boundary promote larger, rounder bubble morphology. Critically, besides gradual bubble growth via trap mutation mechanism, we identify two distinct stress-relief mechanisms: loop punching in anisotropic tilt {\Sigma}5 boundary and interfacial decohesion in twist {\Sigma}11 boundary, with the dominant pathway determined by the interplay between bubble morphology and local mechanical softness. This study establishes a fundamental connection between GB crystallographic and energetical anisotropy and helium bubble evolution, providing critical insights for designing radiation-tolerant microstructures.
item.dc:creator: Yang Zhang, Peter Hatton, Blas P. Uberuaga, Jason R. Trelewicz

item.title: Boltzmann generators for amorphous particle systems
item.description: arXiv:2512.16607v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Sampling configurations in thermodynamic equilibrium is a long-standing challenge in statistical physics. Boltzmann generators address this problem by employing generative models to propose independent configurations, which are then reweighted via importance sampling using exact likelihood evaluations. Recent Boltzmann Generators based on continuous normalizing flows and flow matching have achieved significant success for particle systems and biomolecules. However, these approaches have not been extended to amorphous materials (glasses), for which equilibrium sampling is notoriously slow. Because of their disordered structure, the invariances and geometrical constraints of amorphous materials differ from those of crystals and biomolecules, preventing the direct use of existing generative models. Here, we develop Boltzmann Generators tailored to amorphous materials by building the required equivariances directly into Riemannian stochastic interpolants. Our framework incorporates periodic boundary conditions and particle symmetries using equivariant graph neural networks. Numerical experiments demonstrate that enforcing physical symmetries significantly improves the accuracy of Boltzmann Generators, but also reveal an intrinsic limitation of the continuous-flow formulation: accumulated numerical errors during likelihood integration break time-reversibility, compromising exact thermodynamic reweighting. These results reveal a fundamental challenge for continuous-flow generative models in statistical mechanics and call for alternative approaches that preserve exact thermodynamic consistency.
item.dc:creator: Louis Grenioux, Leonardo Galliano, Ludovic Berthier, Giulio Biroli, Marylou Gabri\'e

item.title: When is vaccine prioritization worth optimizing?
item.description: arXiv:2607.00484v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Optimizing vaccine prioritization is often treated as the default policy response when vaccine supply is limited. Yet optimized prioritization carries administrative, ethical and communication costs, motivating an upstream question: whether differences among vaccine allocations can alter epidemic outcomes enough to make optimization epidemiologically necessary. We show that optimization is not always worth pursuing: in some regimes, vaccination markedly reduces epidemic burden, but many feasible allocation rules perform almost equally well, making the necessity of optimization low. We quantify this necessity as the range of epidemic outcomes generated by different allocations under fixed supply and show that it is governed by competition between vaccinating high-contact groups to slow transmission and vaccinating groups that benefit most directly: necessity is low when these protection routes are balanced and high when one dominates. Increasing transmission intensity changes this balance and drives a transition in the optimal allocation from transmission-focused prioritization toward direct protection. Different prevention objectives exhibit distinct transition thresholds, creating regimes in which optimizing one objective substantially compromises another, thereby revealing when the choice of prevention target matters most. This framework reframes vaccine prioritization as a prior decision problem, identifying when optimization is warranted, when simpler rules suffice, and when prevention goals conflict.
item.dc:creator: Mi Feng, Zhaohua Lin, Changsong Zhou, Liang Tian

item.title: Electronic Properties of Ladder-Type Phenylenes Studied by Thermally-Assisted-Occupation Density Functional Theory
item.description: arXiv:2610.09783v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Accurate prediction of the electronic properties of extended $\pi$-conjugated systems with radical character remains a major theoretical challenge. To overcome this challenge, thermally-assisted-occupation density functional theory (TAO-DFT) has been developed in recent years. In this study, we employ TAO-DFT to systematically explore the electronic properties of ladder-type phenylenes ($n$-LPs), containing $n$ linearly fused four-membered carbon rings. Our calculations reveal that all investigated $n$-LPs (with $n$ = 1 ~ 40) possess singlet ground states. With increasing $n$-LP length, we observe a transition from the nonradical character of shorter $n$-LPs to the polyradical character of longer $n$-LPs. Notably, we identify a distinct damped periodic oscillation in the radical character of $n$-LPs, featuring highly correlated hotspots at specific lengths ($n = 3k - 1$, where $k$ are positive integers). The real-space representation of active orbitals confirms this global electronic behavior is governed by the intrinsic structural periodicity and completely delocalized nature of the active orbitals along the central ladder framework. These findings provide fundamental insights into the size-dependent electronic properties of $n$-LPs, guiding their rational design for future nanomaterial applications.
item.dc:creator: Tsu-Hsuan Wang, Jeng-Da Chai
